bullets.title: META settles youth-harm lawsuits for up to $16.68B; $10B Q3 charge flagged
bullets.body: Meta reached a settlement with 48 states over allegations its platforms harmed children, agreeing to pay a maximum of $16.68B over 10 years. The company will accrue ~$10B in Q3 2026 for the settlement. Evercore ISI reiterated Outperform with $860 PT, framing the settlement as removing existential legal risk (potential adverse verdicts could have approached $1.4T). Fintwit consensus noted the settlement cost is a rounding error vs. Meta's AI capex, and the under-18 cohort is not a large revenue driver; DM features are excluded from restrictions.

bullets.title: NVDA earnings: $110B whisper vs. $92.3B consensus; tech ended 7-day losing streak
bullets.body: Nvidia reports after the bell with a 5% expected move; the unofficial whisper number is ~$110B vs. $92.3B Street consensus. Goldman's flows desk flagged notable 'tech de-risking sequencing' ahead of results. Separately, tech ended a 7-day losing streak (longest since summer 2022) the prior session. Historically, NVDA has beaten estimates 4 straight quarters but shares dropped each time, raising caution about the buy-the-news trade.

bullets.title: July PCE runs hot: headline beats at +0.2% m/m / 3.7% y/y; core steady at 3.3%
bullets.body: July PCE came in at +0.2% m/m vs. +0.1% expected (+3.7% y/y vs. +3.6% est.), while core PCE matched at +0.2% m/m / 3.3% y/y—now 65 consecutive months above the Fed's 2% target. Capital Economics says the print is unlikely to force a September hike but higher rates may eventually be needed. More than half of the core PCE gain was driven by portfolio-management fees tied to equity price gains, not broad goods/services inflation.

bullets.title: OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC claims performance edge over Nvidia GB300; CUDA moat questioned
bullets.body: OpenAI's Jalapeño ASIC, equipped with HBM4, is claimed to outperform Nvidia's GB300 (HBM3E), though the memory-generation gap makes direct comparison unfair; Vera Rubin and Helios are flagged as better future benchmarks. Separately, Tensordyne claims agentic AI can now auto-generate kernels, potentially eroding CUDA's software moat for inference. Chinese GLM-5.3-Flash model is reported serving 100T tokens/day on domestic Ascend chips at per-token costs comparable to Nvidia GPUs.

bullets.title: Custom silicon race heats up: Meta MTIA 300, Google TPU v10, AMD secure SOC at Hot Chips
bullets.body: Hot Chips 2026 Day 2 highlighted AMD framing its secure-computing adaptive SOC around three architectural pillars targeting physical AI, data center, and mission-critical systems. Google presented TPU v10, and Meta's MTIA 300 advances its custom silicon strategy. Advanced packaging cited as far from mature optimization across the industry.

bullets.title: Anthropic to spend $45B on NScale compute powered by future NVIDIA chips; secures 460MW
bullets.body: Anthropic has agreed to lease NScale's data center for $45B and will receive 460 megawatts of power from the facility. OpenAI and Anthropic together are consuming one-third of incremental global compute supply, a share expected to rise to ~50% next year. SoftBank is also mulling a $20B bond sale to fund its OpenAI stake.

bullets.title: 5Y Treasury auction tails for 10th/15th consecutive time; yields hit session highs
bullets.body: The 5-year Treasury auction tailed for the 10th consecutive time (high yield 4.393% vs. WI 4.391%), with one account noting this is actually the 15th consecutive failure to stop through. Yields hit session highs following weak demand, with foreign buyers continuing to reduce Treasury purchases.

bullets.title: Core PCE inflation: services ex-housing at 3.8% y/y; comparisons get harder into year-end
bullets.body: July core PCE breakdown: core goods +0.15% m/m / 2.3% y/y; housing +0.26% / 3.2% y/y; core services ex-housing +0.28% / 3.8% y/y. Monthly annualized rate is ~3%. Year-over-year comparisons for core PCE tighten significantly Aug–Nov 2025 (prior readings 0.18–0.23%), making progress toward 2% target harder.

bullets.title: Q2 GDP confirmed at +1.5%; personal consumption beats at +3.4% vs. +3.2% est.
bullets.body: The second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP held at +1.5% q/q annualized, matching expectations. Personal consumption came in stronger at +3.4% vs. +3.2% estimate. Durable goods orders also beat at +1.1% m/m vs. +0.5% expected, though ex-transportation and cap goods orders missed.

bullets.title: AVGO oversold at key support; LITE flagged as high-quality AI play post-bottleneck-trade shift
bullets.body: AVGO is flagged as short-term oversold testing key support, with NVDA earnings as a potential bounce catalyst. LITE is highlighted as continuing its upward trajectory as the market shifts from indiscriminate AI infrastructure plays to quality names, per the Gavin Baker thesis that the 'AI bottleneck trade' has ended.

bullets.title: AMD 'higher low' pattern firming up technically
bullets.body: AMD is described as displaying a firming 'higher low' pattern on charts, seen as a constructive technical setup, while AVGO tests support and NVDA earnings loom as the near-term catalyst for the broader semiconductor group.

bullets.title: TTMI insider buying: CEO puts in $1.1M, director adds $525K ahead of NVDA earnings
bullets.body: TTM Technologies CEO invested $1.1M in company shares, while director Rex Geveden loaded $525K the prior day, both purchases occurring ~17% off recent highs and timed just before Nvidia's earnings report—framed as a strong insider confidence signal in AI infrastructure adjacency.

bullets.title: MU: former TSM chairman's $8M buy at ATH now up 177% — insider conviction revisited
bullets.body: The former chairman of TSMC purchased $8M of Micron at all-time highs; shares have since risen 177%. The anecdote is being circulated as evidence that insider conviction buys at highs can generate significant alpha, particularly in AI memory infrastructure names.

bullets.title: MU names Manish Bhatia COO and President
bullets.body: Micron announced Manish Bhatia as its new COO and President in a leadership reshuffle. No further details on strategic implications were provided in social commentary.

bullets.title: DDR memory supply chain 'cascading bottlenecks': ODMs downgrading to DDR2 amid DDR4 shock
bullets.body: ODMs are redesigning systems downward from DDR4 to DDR3 to DDR2 due to supply shocks and cost pressures, while legacy suppliers like Winbond are withdrawing from DDR2 production. Q2/Q3 DDR2 pricing showed an enormous hike. A separate Kioxia ¥1 trillion memory plant investment signals broad capacity expansion ahead.

bullets.title: AAPL iPhone 18 launch event confirmed for September 9th; IDC forecasts 10M foldable units in year 1
bullets.body: Apple sent out official invites for its iPhone 18 release event on September 9th at 1PM ET. IDC separately predicts Apple will sell 10 million foldable iPhones in the first year of availability.

bullets.title: AMZN acquires DuckLabs to enhance AWS analytics capabilities
bullets.body: Amazon announced an agreement to acquire DuckLabs (makers of DuckDB), bringing database engineering expertise to AWS with a stated goal of making analytics faster, simpler, and more cost-effective. DuckDB will remain free and open source under the DuckDB Foundation.

bullets.title: Intel 18A-P achieves 30% frequency gain on production silicon; roadmap intact
bullets.body: Intel's 18A-P process node delivers a 30% frequency improvement at 0.5V on production silicon and will power the Diamond Rapids and Nova Lake CPU platforms, providing a concrete data point that the 18A roadmap is on track.

bullets.title: SPY $2B+ put wall at 765 keeps market pinned; positive gamma noted in single stocks
bullets.body: Options flow commentary flags a $2B+ put wall at SPY strike 765 that has kept price pinned throughout the week. Separately, positive gamma support is noted for SPX and aggregate single stocks, providing a mechanical floor ahead of NVDA earnings.

bullets.title: AI economics will ultimately shift toward application layer, not infrastructure
bullets.body: Historical analogy from desktop and internet eras: while AI infrastructure (compute, hyperscalers) currently captures most economics, the greatest margins ultimately accrued to companies closest to end users. The question is when—not if—this margin shift occurs in AI. Open-source model share rising from 28% to 62% of token usage accelerates this pressure.
